heading: A Penticton & Naramata Wine Weekend
title: Penticton & Naramata Wine Weekend | Okanagan Roam
description: A two-day Penticton and Naramata wine weekend: Bench tastings and a winery lunch, then the lakefront, the KVR trail, breweries and dinner downtown.
intro: This weekend splits in two. Day 1 is a slow drive along Naramata Road, tasting your way across the Naramata Bench with a long winery lunch in the middle. Day 2 stays in Penticton: a lakefront brunch and walk, a stretch of the Kettle Valley Rail Trail, a brewery hop and dinner downtown. Everything is a short drive apart, so pick a designated driver or book a tour for the wine day.

Many tasting rooms cut their hours from November to April, and some close on weekdays or shut for the season, so check each listing's hours before you set out. If this is your first time touring wineries, start with our {page:/guides/okanagan-wineries-first-timers|first-timer's guide}. For a custom plan built around your own dates, try the {page:/trip|trip planner}.

sections.heading: Day 1 morning: up onto the Naramata Bench
sections.lead: Fuel up at the foot of the Bench, then start tasting when the wineries open.

items.name: Bench Market
items.text: a popular cafeteria-style breakfast and market spot, and a handy pitstop before a Naramata Bench wine day. The gluten-free options are excellent, and dogs are welcome on the terrace.

items.name: Laughing Stock Vineyards
items.text: an award-winning winery high on a hill, with a terrace overlooking the lake. Try the playful blind-tasting format, and don't miss the chardonnay and syrah.

items.name: Lang Vineyards
items.text: a patio overlooking the lake, and tastings are free. Among the reds, look for the marechal foch.

items.name: Red Rooster Winery
items.text: a well-known Bench winery with a wide-ranging list and knowledgeable, unpushy staff. Reservations are recommended but not required. From fall to spring the wine shop opens Friday to Sunday only, which suits a weekend.

sections.heading: Day 1 afternoon: a winery lunch and more tastings
sections.lead: Book lunch ahead. For more winery kitchens across the valley, see our {page:/guides/okanagan-winery-restaurants|winery restaurants guide}.

items.name: Poplar Grove Winery
items.text: a patio with a standout view and a kitchen that holds its own against the wine list. The food isn't an afterthought, so plan on a proper meal.

items.name: Serendipity Winery
items.text: a tiny, one-chef bistro and winery with a covered, heated patio, so the weather rarely gets in the way. Booking ahead is essential.

items.name: Township 7 Vineyards & Winery
items.text: known for detailed, unhurried tastings. The fee is waived when you buy a bottle.

items.name: Elephant Island Winery
items.text: berry and apricot fruit wines made in an orchard setting on the Aikins Loop. A change of pace from grape wines, poured with family warmth.

sections.heading: Day 1 evening: a late pour and dinner in the village
sections.lead: Most tasting rooms close by late afternoon. These two keep the day going.

items.name: Little Engine Wines
items.text: one of the few Naramata Road wineries that keeps its spacious patio open past 5pm, with great views. An easy way to stretch the wine day after other rooms have closed.

items.name: Bistro Lapin Perdu
items.text: a quiet, romantic French bistro inside the historic Naramata Inn, with a garden view. It's built for slow conversation, course by course, so book ahead.

sections.heading: Day 2 morning: the Penticton lakefront
sections.lead: Day 2 stays in town. Start with brunch by the water, then walk or ride it off.

items.name: Elma
items.text: a beachfront Turkish restaurant with an exceptional weekend brunch. Book it.

items.name: Okanagan Beach
items.text: nearly a kilometre of sand along Lakeshore Drive, beside the SS Sicamous. Free parking and nearby washrooms (the universal washroom is open year-round) make it an easy walk in any season. Dogs aren't permitted.

items.name: Penticton Ikeda Japanese Garden
items.text: a quiet garden on the Okanagan Lake waterfront, with koi ponds and graceful bridges. It's a lovely pause on a lakeside stroll near the S.S. Sicamous, and the plantings bloom in April and May.

items.name: KVR Trail: Skaha Lake, Penticton to Okanagan Falls
items.text: the south spur of the Kettle Valley Rail Trail, flat and easy packed gravel with the lake beside you the whole way. Pick it up at the far end of Wright's Beach Camp off Skaha Lake Road and do a shorter out-and-back. Pioneer Park along the way has a beach, washrooms and parking for a break.

sections.heading: Day 2 afternoon: a brewery hop
sections.lead: Three taprooms close together, so you can walk between the last two.

items.name: Tin Whistle Brewing
items.text: calls itself the Okanagan's original microbrewery, in the historic Cannery Trade Centre, a former fruit cannery. The Peach Cream Ale is always on tap, and records spin in the background.

items.name: Highway 97 Brewing
items.text: consistently well-crafted beer, and travellers with dogs are welcome. Order the pulled pork nachos, then walk across the street to Cannery.

items.name: Cannery Brewing
items.text: a family-friendly main taproom with shareable snacks and a wide range of craft beer. Its Backyard patio closes for the off-season, and dogs aren't allowed in the taproom.

sections.heading: Day 2 evening: cocktails and a winery dinner downtown
sections.lead: End the weekend back on the wine theme, without leaving town.

items.name: Wildflower Distilling Co.
items.text: a downtown craft distillery that doubles as an intimate cocktail lounge, with house-made gins and vodkas. Start with a tasting flight, then let the bartender take it from there.

items.name: Chronos Winery
items.text: a downtown winery that does dinner theatre right, with Caesar salad made tableside and a cellar tour that includes bottle-sabring. The full dinner menu stays open late, so stay for the meal after the tour.

sections.heading: If the weather turns
sections.lead: Indoor options in Penticton for a wet or cold afternoon. Check hours, since some close on Sundays or for private events.

items.name: SS Sicamous Museum & Heritage Park
items.text: a restored 1914 sternwheeler beached at the west end of Okanagan Beach. Wander the cabins, dining saloon and wheelhouse. It closes for private events on some days, especially Saturdays, so check before you go.

items.name: Penticton Art Gallery
items.text: a public gallery on the waterfront by Okanagan Beach, with rotating exhibitions across several rooms. Admission is about $10 for adults.

items.name: Shelter Floating Sauna
items.text: a cedar sauna floating on Okanagan Lake at the Lakeside Resort marina. Cycle between heat, a cold lake plunge and rest in a 70-minute session booked online ahead.

items.name: Upper Bench Estate Winery and Creamery
items.text: a winery and working creamery in one. Order the cheese pairing with your tasting, and say hello to the resident dogs in the tasting room.

items.tip: stay in Penticton for the easiest drives to both days, or in Naramata for a quieter night close to the wineries.

items.name: Therapy Vineyards
items.text: a winery with a boutique inn, where you get a welcome glass of wine at check-in and heated bathroom floors.
